gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the '4000+ cycles' claims have no end-of-life capacity behind them, and the warranties don't define one either: Allied's RS warranty excludes 'capacity loss, reduced runtime, voltage drop, or performance degradation over time', and LiTime's 5-year 48V warranty covers only units that 'fail to operate', so neither maker guarantees a capacity floor.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited pages, golfcartshowdown.com and golfcartbatterysource.com, and our own dealectric.com page. Golf Cart Showdown gives warranty years and full-replacement periods, and notes that Bolt's warranty ends at 3,000 cycles. It names no capacity threshold for any brand and never says Allied excludes capacity loss. Golf Cart Battery Source lists Allied as '8 years prorated (10 on a new RS if registered)'. It warns about '10,000 cycles' claims but gives no DoD or end-of-life basis for any pack. Our page already says LiTime's '4000+ cycles @100% DOD' has no end-of-life capacity and already converts surge to amp-seconds. It leaves LiTime's warranty out and doesn't mention the LiTime 150Ah. No page has LiTime's 150Ah 300 A / 1000 A for 5 s pack.
decides: This confirms the cheaper picks, LiTime and Vatrer, over the $2,699.99 Allied RS on value. Allied's premium buys no promise against capacity fade: past year 3 its warranty is prorated, and it explicitly excludes degradation. The surge table changes the hill pick. LiTime's 48V 150Ah, at $1,549.99, is rated 300 A continuous and 1,000 A for 5 s. That is 5,000 A·s, against Eco Gen3's 3,000 A·s at $2,671 and LiTime 100Ah's 600 A·s. ChatGPT's 'high-current' advice should point there, not to the 100Ah kit, whose 1C rating means 100 A continuous.

findings.label: Warranty: what counts as a failure
findings.value: 10 years; repair or replace in years 1-3, prorated in years 4-10; capacity loss excluded
findings.source_title: Allied Battery Warranty - Allied Lithium Golf Cart Batteries
findings.note: Excludes 'Capacity loss, reduced runtime, voltage drop, or performance degradation over time' with no numeric threshold. Also excludes end-of-life from 'high-frequency cycling'. Registration within 60 days is required, otherwise coverage is 1 year. Not transferable; continental US only. RS units sold before March 2026 carry 8 years, prorated monthly.

findings.label: Warranty: length and capacity coverage
findings.value: 5 years for new units (3 years for 'Like New'); covers units that 'fail to operate' from a defect; no capacity threshold stated
findings.note: The table row reads '48V series: all capacity range'. The policy has no 70%/80% capacity floor and no cycle limit. The cell is not covered unless the owner fully charges it within 7 days of purchase and at least once every 3 months. Original purchaser only, not transferable.
